# Jubilees Chapter 29 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Jacob departs from Laban; return to Canaan

---

**29:1** And in the first year of the first week of the forty-fifth jubilee, Jacob went to Laban to depart from him to his father's land of Canaan.

**29:2** And Laban called to him all his flocks and all his sons and all his daughters and embraced him and kissed him and wept greatly, and said to Jacob: "I pray thee, do not leave me. I have found favor in thy sight. Stay with me, and God shall bless me because of thee."

**29:3** But Jacob would not stay, but said to Laban: "Let me go, for my father waits for me and my mother; release me that I may go."

**29:4** And Laban departed from him with weeping, and Jacob went on his way.

**29:5** And Jacob sent messengers before him to Esau his brother to the land of Seir.

**29:6** And they returned to Jacob, saying: "We came to thy brother Esau and he is coming to meet thee with four hundred men."

**29:7** And Jacob was exceedingly afraid, and he divided his people and his flocks and his cattle and his camels into two bands.

**29:8** And he said: "If Esau comes to the one band and smites it, then the other band which is left shall escape."

**29:9** And Jacob prayed to the LORD his God: "O God of my father Abraham and God of my father Isaac, O LORD, who didst say to me: 'Return to thy land and to thy kindred, and I will deal well with thee.'

**29:10** I am not worthy of all the mercies and of all the faithfulness which thou hast shown to thy servant; for with my staff alone I crossed this Jordan, and now I have become two bands.

**29:11** Deliver me, I pray thee, from the hand of my brother Esau, for I fear him, lest he come and smite me, the mothers with the children.

**29:12** And thou didst say: 'I will surely do thee good, and make thy seed as the sand of the sea, which cannot be numbered for multitude.'"

**29:13** And Jacob lodged there that night. And he took from that which came to his hand a present for his brother Esau: two hundred she-goats and twenty he-goats, two hundred ewes and twenty rams, thirty milk-camels with their colts, forty cows and ten bulls, twenty she-asses and ten foals.

**29:14** And he gave them into the hand of his servants, every drove by itself, and said to his servants: "Pass over before me and put a space between drove and drove."

**29:15** And he commanded the foremost: "When Esau my brother meets thee and asks thee: 'Whose art thou and whither dost thou go, and whose are these before thee?'

**29:16** Then thou shalt say: 'They are thy servant Jacob's; it is a present sent to my lord Esau; and behold, he is also behind us.'"

**29:17** And Jacob was left alone. And there wrestled with him a man until the dawn.

**29:18** And when he saw that he prevailed not against him, he struck the socket of his hip; and the socket of Jacob's hip was strained as he wrestled with him.

**29:19** And he said: "Let me go, for the dawn has come up." And he said: "I will not let thee go except thou bless me."

**29:20** And he said to him: "What is thy name?" And he said: "Jacob." And he said: "Thy name shall no more be called Jacob, but Israel; for thou hast striven with God and with men, and hast prevailed."

**29:21** And Jacob asked and said: "Tell me, I pray thee, thy name." And he said: "Why is it that thou askest after my name?" And he blessed him there.

**29:22** And Jacob called the name of that place Peniel — "the face of God" — for he said: "I have seen God face to face, and yet my life is preserved."

**29:23** And the sun rose upon him as he passed Penuel, and he was limping upon his thigh.

**29:24** Therefore the children of Israel do not eat the sinew of the hip which is upon the socket of the hip, to this day.

---

*EMET notes: Jubilees' version of the wrestling and the Jacob-Esau reconciliation compresses the Genesis 32-33 material and inserts the jubilee chronology. "Peniel/Penuel" alternation follows the Ge'ez text. The sinew prohibition (v.24) is given as an etiology in both Genesis and Jubilees.*
